messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PAGER -> kv-cache-eviction spike in region-us-east-1. p95 latency > 600ms. Incident ID INC-20240424-987. Pager count: 3.
maya: i'm on it — joining bridge. sahil, can you ack/come in?
sahil: ack, joining bridge in 30s. what's the immediate customer impact?
maya: dashboards show increased retry rates for /v1/generate and a small increase in 5xx. Dedicated customers on pool-ded-5 may see degraded tail latency. No full outage reported yet.
alex: jumping into infra — seeing repeated OOMs on one pod in pool-ded-5, causing eviction storms and heavy KV cache churn.
jordan: confirmed. `kubectl describe pod ded-5-rcv4 -n runtime` shows frequent `Evicted` events and kernel OOM lines.
alex: logs snippet:
```
2024-04-24T18:02:11Z runtime[ded-5-rcv4]: kv_cache: evict key=batch_42 size=8MB
2024-04-24T18:02:12Z runtime[ded-5-rcv4]: runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
2024-04-24T18:02:12Z runtime[ded-5-rcv4]: process restarted (OOM)
```
maya: can we cordon that node and spin up replacements? if we drain we might trigger more pods to re-schedule and make a temporary spike.
sahil: plan: 1) divert new traffic off pool-ded-5 to pool-ded-3/4, 2) scale pool-ded-5 replicas up to absorb churn, 3) cordon problematic node for manual inspection. I'll run the routing change now.
sahil: running `redwoodctl route set pool-ded-5 -drain=true --fallback-pool=pool-ded-3` — executing.
incident-bot: ACTION -> route change applied by sahil. Request routing will now send new sessions to pool-ded-3.
alex: scaling pool-ded-5 up: `redwoodctl scale pool pool-ded-5 --replicas 6` to give room for re-schedules and reduce per-pod mem pressure.
alex: scale command accepted, pods are creating. monitoring for OOMs.
jordan: i've attached a short tracing snippet showing increased kv-pop operations correlated with model variant `redwood-model-xl-quant` and long context lengths from a customer workload. Might be a hot-key.
liz: pinging support/CS: any customer-reported incidents? we should surface impacted tenants and let them know mitigation in progress.
maya: support reports 4 customers with elevated latencies, all on dedicated pools. no major user-facing errors at scale. sending a brief update to affected accounts now. :loudspeaker:
oliver: can we get an owner to file a post-incident review? we should capture root cause hypotheses (noisy pod / kv hot-key / model mem pattern) and remediation (runbook, routing safeguards).
maya: i'll take commander for the immediate incident and assign postmortem. sahil — can you follow up on the routing/playbook changes? alex/jordan — infra diagnostics and root cause analysis.
sahil: yes, i'll own runbook edits for routing and fallback policies.
alex: i'll look into kernel OOM traces and GPU mem patterns, collect heap profiles. jordan: i'll map which requests/clients correlate with the hot-key.
liz: i'll start the customer communication thread and attach the summary.
maya: temporary mitigation looks stable: eviction rate dropped ~70% after draining and scaling. we'll keep the bridge for 30 more mins then hand off.
incident-bot: NOTE -> 45m elapsed. still monitoring.
maya: Handoff to night oncall (oliver) scheduled at 21:00 UTC. oliver, if everything looks stable please 1) confirm progress, 2) create postmortem doc in /postmortems, 3) own remediation tracking.
oliver: acknowledged. will take over at 21:00 UTC.
maya: immediate action items:
- [A1] sahil: update runbook section "routing-fallbacks" with explicit `redwoodctl` commands and verification steps. due 2024-05-01.
- [A2] alex: collect OOM logs + heap profiles from ded-5 pods and attach to postmortem. due 2024-04-30.
- [A3] jordan: produce per-client request sample and identify hot-key traffic. due 2024-04-30.
- [A4] liz: customer notifications + list of impacted account IDs. due 2024-04-25.
- [A5] oliver: schedule postmortem meeting and create doc skeleton: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-20240424-987 (please create). due 2024-04-26.
maya: temp runbook note: add a quick-check section for kv eviction spikes and a step to divert traffic before cordoning nodes. sahil pls make that explicit.
sahil: will add a short checklist and a cmd block like:
```
# drain pool
redwoodctl route set pool-ded-5 -drain=true --fallback-pool=pool-ded-3
# scale to safety
redwoodctl scale pool pool-ded-5 --replicas 6
# verify
redwoodctl pods --pool pool-ded-5 --watch
```
maya: postmortem owners — i'll assign severity and timeline after oliver creates doc. include timeline with exact timestamps for routing change and scale.
oliver: created postmortem doc (INC-20240424-987) and invited owners. meeting scheduled 2024-04-27 16:00 UTC. calendar link posted in doc.
alex: follow-up: reproducer found: long-context batched calls with model-xl-quant and a specific caching pattern cause KV churn when combined with certain quantization buffers. more analysis incoming.
jordan: +1, will link sample requests to reproducer.
liz: customers notified with status update, CS tickets created for affected accounts.
maya: closing bridge in 10. will leave incident status as "Monitoring". oliver pls run the postmortem and ensure runbook edits land in main before next release.
incident-bot: INCIDENT -> status set to MONITORING by maya. bridge closed.
oliver: received handoff. will follow through with PM to prioritize runbook changes and evaluate automating fallback routing on eviction thresholds.
maya: thanks all — nice rapid response. action owners please update the postmortem doc with their notes before due dates. :thumbsup:
oliver: noted, will file follow-up JIRA epics for remediation after the postmortem.
maya: thread closed for follow-ups; please continue updates in the postmortem doc rather than here.
